checkpoints.note: The witness contains a space date/time separator and a `-02` timezone suffix, so `g_date_time_new_from_iso8601()` enters time parsing on `200007.<309 fractional digits>-02`. `parse_iso8601_time()` recognizes the `hhmmss(.sss)` form, strips the timezone into a non-NULL `tz`, and routes the `07.<309 digits>` substring into `get_iso8601_seconds()`.
First project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled long fractional-seconds substring into the parser's `seconds` output.

checkpoints.code:
if (year < 1 || year > 9999 ||
    month < 1 || month > 12 ||
    day < 1 || day > days_in_months[GREGORIAN_LEAP (year)][month] ||
    hour < 0 || hour > 23 ||
    minute < 0 || minute > 59 ||
    seconds < 0.0 || seconds >= 60.0)
  return NULL;
checkpoints.note: For the witness's non-finite `seconds`, both `seconds < 0.0` and `seconds >= 60.0` evaluate false, so the constructor continues into integer-based time calculations instead of rejecting the input. The fix adds `!isfinite (seconds)` here and also hardens `get_iso8601_seconds()`.

The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 2` at `glib/gdatetime.c:2188:16` and says the faulting address is 14 bytes to the left of global `days_in_year` defined at `glib/gdatetime.c:175`. Since `days_in_year[0]` is a 13-entry `guint16` row, that offset corresponds to indexing 7 elements before `days_in_year[0][0]`, i.e. `the_month - 1 == -7` on the crashing execution.
